name: the universe
description: events that happened before there was an earth, or far beyond it.

name: the whole world
description: events that touched the entire planet at once: changes in climate, mass extinctions, pandemics, world wars, and global technology.

name: africa
description: the continent where humans first appeared, home to egypt, kush, aksum, mali, songhai, great zimbabwe, and the swahili coast, and later to the struggle against colonial rule.

name: the middle east
description: mesopotamia, the levant, arabia, persia, and anatolia: the land of the first farms, cities, and writing, and the birthplace of judaism, christianity, and islam.

name: europe
description: from the greeks and romans through medieval kingdoms to the industrial revolution, the world wars, and the european union.

name: south asia
description: the indian subcontinent: the indus valley, the vedic age, the maurya and gupta empires, the mughals, british rule, and independence.

name: east asia
description: china, korea, japan, and mongolia: the dynasties of china, the samurai of japan, and the mongol conquests.

name: southeast asia
description: the lands and islands between india and china, including the khmer empire, srivijaya, and modern indonesia and vietnam.

name: central asia
description: the steppe and the silk roads: the home of horse riders, nomad empires, and the great trading cities of the silk roads.

name: north america
description: from the first people crossing beringia to the mississippian mound builders, european colonies, and the united states.

name: mesoamerica and the caribbean
description: mexico, central america, and the caribbean islands: the olmecs, maya, teotihuacan, and aztecs, then spanish rule and haiti's revolution.

name: south america
description: caral, chavín, the nazca and moche, the inca empire, spanish and portuguese rule, and independence.

name: oceania
description: australia, new guinea, new zealand, and the islands of the pacific, settled by some of the greatest sailors in history.

name: the arctic and antarctica
description: the frozen ends of the earth, the last places humans reached.
